chats.temporaryRetentionHoursHelp: Temporary chats — incognito chats, anonymous visitors' chats, and every chat while the history is off — are deleted this many hours after their last activity, checked hourly. At least 1, at most 720 (30 days).

toolSupport.required: Tools - a tool call can be required

hints.modelId: Unique identifier for the model (cannot be changed after creation)
hints.supportsTools: Whether the model can be given tools, and whether the provider can force it to call one. Pick "a tool call can be required" only if the provider accepts a forced tool choice (OpenAI, Mistral, Google and Bedrock do; Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1 do not; vLLM and other local servers depend on the installation, so keep those on "the model decides"). Apps that require a tool call ask a "the model decides" model in words instead.
hints.apiModelId: Model identifier used by the provider's API (e.g., gpt-4, claude-3-opus)
hints.apiKey: API key for this model. If not provided, the system will use the key of its provider or the environment variable. A local server (vLLM, LM Studio, Jan.ai, Ollama) needs no key — leave this empty. Keys are stored encrypted.
hints.apiKeySet: ✓ API key is configured for this model
hints.supportsVision: Enable if this model can process image inputs
hints.supportsAudio: Enable if this model can process audio inputs
hints.supportsImageGeneration: Enable if this model can generate images (e.g., Gemini Image models)
hints.modelType: Chat models answer prompts. Transcription models convert audio to text via a realtime endpoint (e.g. Voxtral). Text-to-speech models read chat messages aloud (e.g. Voxtral TTS).
hints.realtimeUrl: Endpoint of the transcription service: a vLLM /v1/realtime WebSocket URL, an OpenAI-compatible /audio/transcriptions URL (Whisper with the OpenAI or Local provider), or the provider’s API. It stays server-side and never reaches the browser.
hints.nativeWebSearch: Apps with web search use the provider's built-in search on this model. Turn it off for models or gateways that do not support it; they fall back to Brave Search.
hints.promptCachingOpenAI: Sends a cache key so requests that start with the same prompt reuse OpenAI’s cache. On by default for api.openai.com; turn it off for OpenAI-compatible servers that reject unknown parameters.
hints.promptCachingExplicit: Marks the tools, system prompt and conversation for caching. Cached input costs about a tenth of normal input, but writing it costs a quarter more, so this pays off when the same app is used again within five minutes. Only for models that support prompt caching.
hints.nativeWebSearchToolVersion: Newer versions let Claude filter search results in code before they reach the context window, which saves tokens on search-heavy prompts. Google Cloud and Azure-hosted Foundry only offer the basic version.
hints.nativeWebSearchDynamicFiltering: Runs web search from code execution (Claude 4.6 or later on the Claude API). When off, the newer tool version is called directly.
hints.thinkingEnabled: Ask the model to think before answering. The reasoning is returned separately from the answer; leave off and a reasoning model writes its thinking into the answer text instead.
hints.thinkingLevel: Sent as reasoning_effort (OpenAI, vLLM) or thinkingLevel (Gemini). Servers that do not support it ignore the value — leave on provider default unless the model documents these levels.
hints.thinkingThoughts: Surface the reasoning to users behind the "Show thinking" toggle. Turn off to keep it hidden.
hints.maxOutputTokens: Empty means the default ({{value}}), not unlimited. Reasoning models spend their thinking tokens from this limit, so keep it well above the longest answer you expect.
hints.sampling: Optional. Leave a field empty to use the model's or provider's own default; nothing is sent for it. A value set here applies to every request to this model.
hints.marking: Whether this model marks the text it generates as AI generated. Choose "Provider marks the output" only when the provider confirmed that in writing; iHub cannot check it. While the EU AI Act features are on, every output still gets a provenance record, whatever you choose here.
hints.markingStatementRef: A document name or URL of the provider's written statement. It is only kept as a reference, never opened.
hints.imageMarking: What the provider embeds in the images this model generates (for example SynthID, an invisible watermark, or a C2PA manifest). iHub adds no mark of its own and never re-encodes a generated image, so the provider's mark stays intact. Choose "Provider marks the output" only when the provider confirmed that in writing; iHub cannot detect it and records it as declared, never as detected.
hints.markingIhub: iHub asks vLLM to watermark every answer with the active key and recognises it again through the detector. The detector settings must equal the vLLM server settings. Greedy sampling (temperature 0) and structured output cannot be watermarked and are recorded as not applied.
hints.ttsUrl: Speech endpoint of the provider. It stays server-side and never reaches the browser.

cimd.revokeAllConfirm: Disconnect all {{count}} user(s) from {{name}}? They can reconnect by signing in and consenting again — block the client first if that is not what you want.

proxy.trustedProxiesHelp: Addresses or subnets the proxy connects from, comma-separated (for example loopback, 10.0.0.5 or 10.0.0.0/8). The headers are used only on connections from these addresses. The default, loopback, covers a proxy on the same host or in the same pod; if other local processes (such as a service-mesh sidecar) forward traffic to iHub, set a shared secret as well.
proxy.sharedSecretHelp: A secret the proxy sends in the shared secret header. When set, the headers are used only on requests that carry it. Together with trusted proxies, both must match: for a proxy elsewhere, add its address above or clear the list to rely on the secret alone.

officeIntegration.step1: Copy the manifest URL above or download the manifest.xml file.

officeIntegration.startPageDesc: What the task pane shows after sign-in — and which app answers there. Messages typed on the start page open that app and are sent right away, with the open email and any collected emails as context.
officeIntegration.defaultPageStart: Start page (greeting, chat input and app shortcuts)
officeIntegration.defaultPageHelp: Where the pane lands after sign-in and where the back button in a chat leads. The app list stays one tap away from the start page either way.
officeIntegration.defaultAppHelp: The app whose chat input the start page shows. When unset — or when a user cannot access it — the top-ranked chat app that user can access is used: favorites first, then the default apps below.
officeIntegration.featuredAppsEmpty: No default apps yet — the start page lists apps in their configured order, favorites first.
officeIntegration.featuredAppsHelp: Shown on the start page in this order, right after each user's favorites. Users who cannot access an app never see it. Drag a row or use the arrows to reorder.
officeIntegration.allowedAppsDesc: Which apps the add-in offers. By default a user sees every app their iHub groups allow, exactly as in the web app. Limit the add-in to a few purpose-built apps here. The limit is stored on the add-in’s OAuth client.
officeIntegration.allowedAppsClientMissing: The add-in’s OAuth client could not be found, so its app access cannot be shown. Disable and enable the integration to create it again.
officeIntegration.allowedAppsModeAll: All apps the user can access
officeIntegration.allowedAppsModeAllDesc: No limit from the add-in. Each user sees the apps their groups allow.
officeIntegration.allowedAppsModeLimitedDesc: Users see only the selected apps, and only those their groups allow too. Being on this list never grants access on its own.
officeIntegration.allowedAppsEmptyWarning: Select at least one app before saving. An empty list would mean no limit.
officeIntegration.allowedAppsEmptyError: Select at least one app, or choose "All apps the user can access". An empty list would mean no restriction.
officeIntegration.allowedAppsUnsaved: Unsaved change. It applies when you click Save at the bottom of the page.
officeIntegration.allowedAppsLiveHint: Takes effect for signed-in users right away. No sign-in or manifest redeploy is needed.
officeIntegration.allowedAppsModelsHint: Models and prompts can be limited the same way on the OAuth client.
officeIntegration.startPageOutsideList: Not in the available apps above, so the task pane will not show: {{apps}}. Add them there, or pick other apps.
officeIntegration.officeJsDesc: Where the add-in loads the Office JavaScript library from. Change this if your network blocks Microsoft’s CDN. Office.js loads the rest of the library relative to this URL, so one setting covers the whole library.
officeIntegration.officeJsModeCdnDesc: Clients load Office.js straight from Microsoft. Always current, and the only option Microsoft AppSource accepts.
officeIntegration.officeJsModeProxyDesc: This server fetches Office.js from the CDN and caches it. Clients never contact Microsoft — only this server needs outbound access, and the cached copy stays up to date.
officeIntegration.officeJsModeCustomDesc: Load from a URL you control — a corporate CDN or an artifact proxy mirroring the Microsoft CDN. Neither clients nor this server need access to Microsoft.
officeIntegration.officeJsModeBundledDesc: Serve the copy shipped with this release. Needs no network at all, but never receives updates.
officeIntegration.officeJsCdnUrlHint: Must end in /office.js. Pick a known CDN below, or paste another.
officeIntegration.officeJsCustomUrlHint: Must end in /office.js — Office.js derives the path to every other file it needs from this URL, and cannot find them without that filename. Point this at a pull-through mirror of the Microsoft CDN.
officeIntegration.officeJsAppSourceWarning: Microsoft AppSource requires add-ins to load Office.js from the official CDN. Any other source is supported for internal enterprise deployments only — which is what sideloading or Microsoft 365 admin center deployment does.
officeIntegration.officeJsBundledWarning: The bundled copy comes from the @microsoft/office-js npm package, which Microsoft no longer maintains. It never updates — including for security fixes — and adds roughly 86 MB to the build. Prefer Proxy or Custom CDN, and use Bundled only where the server has no outbound access at all.
officeIntegration.officeJsKnownCdnsDesc: Checks each URL from this server and from your browser. The server result is what the Proxy mode needs; the browser result is the closer stand-in for an Outlook client, which loads Office.js itself in the Microsoft CDN and Custom modes.
officeIntegration.officeJsFallbackWarning: The saved Office.js source could not be used, so the add-in is falling back to {{mode}}. Check the URL above.
officeIntegration.mailActionDesc: What the button under each assistant answer does in Outlook. Every action stays available in the button’s menu — this only picks the one that needs no extra tap.
officeIntegration.defaultMailActionHelp: Users can override this per device in the task pane’s Settings dialog. A choice Outlook cannot offer for the open item falls back to one it can — pick Reply all and a user composing a draft still gets Insert.
officeIntegration.mailActionAuto: Automatic — reply all in the reading pane, insert while composing
officeIntegration.addinIdShared: Every iHub installation ships this ID. Generate a new one to install this server next to another one (for example dev and production) in the same Outlook.
officeIntegration.regenerateAddinIdConfirm: Outlook treats a manifest with a new ID as a different add-in. Everyone using the add-in must install the new manifest, and the old one keeps pointing at this server until it is removed. Continue?
officeIntegration.regenerateAddinIdDone: New add-in ID generated. Download the manifest and deploy it again.

ssrf.title: SSRF Allowlist
ssrf.description: Allow outbound HTTP calls (OpenAPI tools, MCP servers, web tools) to reach intentionally internal services even when their hostname resolves to a private IP. Short links may also lead only to websites whose host is on this list.

proxy.enabled: Use a proxy for outbound requests

cookieSettings.description: Configure cookie security settings for authentication
cookieSettings.disableSecureDesc: When enabled, removes the 'secure' flag from authentication cookies. This allows cookies to work over HTTP connections without SSL. Only enable this for internal deployments without SSL.
cookieSettings.securityWarningDesc: Disabling the secure cookie flag allows cookies to be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections. This makes your authentication tokens vulnerable to interception. Only use this in secure, internal network environments without SSL.
cookieSettings.defaultBehavior: By default, cookies are marked as secure in production environments, which means they will only be sent over HTTPS connections. This is the recommended security setting.

rateLimits.title: Rate limits
rateLimits.description: How many requests one client address may send before it gets "429 Too Many Requests". Changes apply after a server restart.
rateLimits.restartRequired: The saved limits differ from the ones the server is running with. Restart the server to apply them.
rateLimits.perAddress: Limits count per client address. Behind a reverse proxy, set the number of proxy hops (trustProxy in platform.json); otherwise every user shares the proxy's address and one counter.
rateLimits.saved: Rate limits saved. Restart the server to apply them.
rateLimits.saveError: Failed to save the rate limits
rateLimits.loadError: Failed to load the rate limits
rateLimits.invalid: {{name}}: enter a whole number of requests from 1 to 1,000,000 and a period from one second to 1,440 minutes.

users.groupMembershipDescription: Assign this user to groups to control their permissions and access levels
users.deleteConfirm: Delete this user? Their access ends immediately, and their API keys, connections, stored credentials, scheduled tasks, chats, prompts, skills and short links are removed. aiAcknowledgement.removeAllMessage: {{count}} confirmations will be removed and everyone, anonymous visitors included, is asked again at their next message. Export the CSV first if you need the list. The audit log keeps the history.

logging.jsonDescription: Structured JSON logging for parsing and analysis

logging.auditAnonymizeIpHelp: Applies to the `ip` field on each audit entry.

logging.note1: Changes take effect immediately across all server processes

gateway.title: MCP gateway (inbound)
gateway.subtitle: Expose iHub tools, apps, and workflows over the Model Context Protocol so MCP-aware clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, agents) can use them as tools.
gateway.enableDesc: When enabled, /mcp accepts OAuth-authenticated requests from external MCP clients. The endpoint is always 404 when disabled.
gateway.consentDesc: Show the OAuth consent screen on authorization_code flow before issuing an MCP-scoped access token.
gateway.publicUrlDesc: Announced in .well-known metadata so MCP-aware clients can auto-discover the endpoint. Leave empty to derive it from the request origin.
gateway.transportStreamableHttpDesc: Canonical MCP HTTP transport per spec 2025-03-26+. Supports session resumption via Mcp-Session-Id + Last-Event-ID.
gateway.transportA2aDesc: Serve an Agent Card at /.well-known/agent-card.json and mount /a2a alongside /mcp, behind the same OAuth + mcp:* scope gate (personal API keys work too). Apps and workflows become the agent's skills; supports message/send, message/stream, tasks/get and tasks/cancel.
gateway.exposeDesc: Resource families surfaced via MCP. Per-OAuth-client allowlists further restrict what an individual caller sees.
gateway.exposeResourcesDesc: Sources / skills surfaced as MCP resources (resources/list + resources/read). Requires scope mcp:resources:read.
gateway.authSectionDesc: The MCP gateway only accepts OAuth bearer tokens issued by the built-in authorization server. It must be enabled for any MCP client to connect.
gateway.oauthWarning: The gateway is enabled but the OAuth authorization server is off — MCP clients cannot obtain a token. Enable it below.
gateway.oauthToggleDesc: Serves /api/oauth/authorize and /api/oauth/token. Enabling this also switches on OAuth client management and the authorization_code + refresh_token grants. A server restart is required after enabling it for the first time.
gateway.dcrToggleDesc: Lets MCP clients register their OAuth client at /api/oauth/register (RFC 7591). Identical public registrations are de-duplicated onto one record, and registered clients always go through user sign-in and consent with identity + mcp:* scopes only.
gateway.claudeHintDcr: Claude: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, then paste the endpoint URL above. Claude registers its OAuth client automatically; users sign in to iHub and consent to the requested mcp:* scopes. Turn on Client ID Metadata Documents above to stop it registering at all.
gateway.claudeHintManual: Claude: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, then paste the endpoint URL above and enter the client ID of an OAuth client you created under /admin/oauth/clients (public client, grant types authorization_code + refresh_token, redirect URI https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback, plus the desired mcp:* scopes). Turn on Client ID Metadata Documents above to skip the manual client setup.
gateway.clientIdSectionDesc: How an MCP client tells iHub who it is. A client picks the first option it can use, so leaving both on gives clients that support metadata documents the stable identity and everything else the legacy path.
gateway.cimdToggleDesc: The client's ID is an HTTPS URL pointing at a metadata document it publishes, so nothing is stored here — one stable identity for every user instead of a new client record per connection. Only the trusted hosts below are accepted, and users always sign in and consent.
gateway.cimdHostsDesc: Comma-separated hostnames whose metadata documents are accepted. Supports *.example.com for subdomains. An empty list accepts nobody; "*" accepts any HTTPS client and is not recommended.
gateway.claudeHintCimd: Claude: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, then paste the endpoint URL above. Claude identifies itself with its metadata document at claude.ai — no client record is created here — and users sign in to iHub and consent to the requested mcp:* scopes.
gateway.claudeHintEnterprise: Claude Team/Enterprise: an organisation admin can instead pin one pre-registered client for everyone — create a public OAuth client with the callback URL above and have them enter its client ID under the connector’s advanced settings.
gateway.cimdBlockedHostsDesc: Comma-separated hostnames that are refused even while they are trusted above, checked before any request leaves this server. Use it to cut off a vendor without editing the trusted list you want to keep. Blocking an individual client is done per client under OAuth → Clients.
gateway.cimdApprovalModeDesc: A trusted host publishes several different clients — Claude web, Claude Desktop, Claude Code — under one hostname. Requiring approval means each one waits for you: the user is told to ask an administrator, and the client appears here as pending. Clients people are already connected through are unaffected.
gateway.a2aDefaultSkillDesc: The app or workflow a message runs when the A2A client names none, as app__<appId> or workflow__<workflowId>. Clients can always choose a skill with metadata.skillId or by using the per-skill endpoint /a2a/skills/<skillId>. Leave empty to require a choice (a caller with exactly one skill needs none).

telemetry.title: Telemetry & Observability
telemetry.description: Configure OpenTelemetry instrumentation following the Gen-AI semantic conventions. Spans, events and metrics can be exported to console, Prometheus or any OTLP-compatible backend (Jaeger, Tempo, Grafana, ...).
telemetry.saveSuccess: Telemetry configuration saved. Some changes (provider, exporter, enabled) require a restart.
telemetry.providerOtlp: Push to an OTLP-compatible collector (Jaeger, Tempo, Grafana, OTel collector)
telemetry.providerPrometheus: Expose Prometheus metrics endpoint for scraping
telemetry.otlpEndpointHelp: Base URL for the OTLP/HTTP collector. /v1/traces and /v1/metrics are appended.
telemetry.promHelp: Metrics will be available at http://{host}:{port}/metrics for Prometheus to scrape.
telemetry.metrics: Emit metrics (token usage, durations, app/conversation counters, active users/chats)
telemetry.events: Emit gen_ai events (prompts, completions, tool calls)
telemetry.privacyWarn: Including prompts and completions may capture PII or sensitive data. Disabled by default.
telemetry.activitySummaryDescription: Periodically log the number of distinct active users and chats observed in a rolling window. Counts are also exposed as the OpenTelemetry observable gauges ihub.active.users and ihub.active.chats.
telemetry.saveDescription: Privacy/event/activity-summary changes apply immediately. Toggling enabled, exporter or provider requires a server restart.
telemetry.refEnvHint: Standard OTEL_* environment variables (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, ...) are honored at startup.
telemetry.refMetricsHint: Custom iHub metrics: ihub.app.usage, ihub.prompt.usage, ihub.errors, ihub.conversations, ihub.active.users, ihub.active.chats.

modelReview.body: Models from the marketplace bring their own settings, including the endpoint URL. Testing or using the model sends the API key it uses (its own or, when it has none, the provider key) and the prompts to that endpoint, so check the URL and settings first.

edit.autoStartHelp: When enabled, the app will automatically start the conversation when the chat is opened or reset
edit.startFormHelp: A new chat opens with these variables as a form instead of the chat input, with a message field, a model selector when users may pick the model, and a drop zone for files when uploads are enabled. Sending the form fills the prompt template once and sends it as the first message; the conversation then continues without the template.
edit.variablesPanelPinned: Pin the input parameters by default
edit.variablesPanelPinnedHelp: Pinned, the input parameters stay open beside the chat. Unpinned, they collapse each time a message is sent and can be expanded again. Users can collapse, expand and pin the panel themselves; this sets where it starts.
edit.ephemeralHelp: When enabled, the chat is never stored. Messages exist only while the chat is open and are discarded when you switch apps or reload.
edit.testHint: Chat with the saved app next to the editor
edit.openDisabledHint: Enable the app and save to open it

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.desc: Bind installed integrations. Narrow them to some actions, and set the scope users start with.
integrations.noActions: This installation offers no action right now.
integrations.notInstalledHelp: This installation no longer exists, so the app is hidden from users. Unbind it to offer the app again.
integrations.notInstalledOptionalHelp: This installation no longer exists. The app stays available without it; unbind it to tidy up.
integrations.requiredHelp: Hide the app while this integration is disabled or missing. Off: the app stays available without its actions.
integrations.enabledByDefaultHelp: New chats start with this integration switched on. Off: it is only available, and users switch it on in the chat's "+" menu when they need it.
integrations.alwaysLoadedHelp: Always send this integration's tools to the model in full. Off: when the app's tools are too many for one request, the model finds them with a search instead.
integrations.pinnedHelp: Fixes the scope; users cannot change it.
integrations.allInstallationsHelp: Every installation of this integration, including ones installed later ({{count}} now).
integrations.explicitAction: Only when ticked here; never part of "every action".
integrations.allOfTypeHelp: Every installation of this kind, including ones installed later ({{count}} now).
integrations.panelNotInstalled: {{name}} is not installed. Install it under Integrations to use these settings.
integrations.peopleDirectoriesDesc: Let the model look people up in the directories: all of them, or single ones.
integrations.storageRequiredHelp: Hide the app while this storage provider is disabled or missing. Off: the app stays available and the file picker offers the providers that are there.
integrations.storageProvidersDesc: Let users pick files for the chat from the storage providers: all of them, or single ones. Users see the ones their groups grant; picked files follow the upload settings.
integrations.typeOverrideHelp: Tick one to give it settings of its own; the others follow the settings above.
integrations.typePickHelp: The app uses only the ones ticked here.
integrations.disabledHidden: Disabled integrations are not offered here ({{count}}). Enable one under Integrations to bind it to this app.

edit.websearchDesc: Configure web search capabilities for this app
edit.websearchProviderDesc: Models with native search (Google, OpenAI, Anthropic) search themselves when Use Native Search is on; no engine is needed for that. On other models the app uses this engine. Auto takes the first engine the user may use: Brave, Staan, Qwant, then any other engine.
edit.websearchEngineMissing: The engine "{{engine}}" is not installed. The app searches natively where the model can and not at all on other models. Install it under Integrations or pick Auto.
edit.websearchEngineDisabled: The engine "{{engine}}" is disabled. Until it is enabled, the app searches natively where the model can and not at all on other models.
edit.websearchNoEngine: No search engine is installed: the app searches only on models with native search.
edit.websearchUseNativeDesc: Use the model's built-in search when available (e.g. Google, OpenAI, Anthropic)
edit.websearchExtractContentDesc: Fetch and extract full page content from search results
edit.websearchMaxSearchesDesc: Caps how many searches the model may run per call with native search (Anthropic bills each search). 1–50, default 5.
edit.websearchResearchGuidanceDesc: Tells the model to run several searches, check sources and combine the findings, instead of answering after one search
edit.websearchResearchGuidanceCustomDesc: Optional. Replaces the built-in guidance that is added to the system prompt when web search is on. Leave empty to use the built-in guidance.
edit.websearchEnabledByDefaultDesc: Whether web search is turned on by default for users
edit.websearchRequiredDesc: Hide the app while its search engine is not available (Auto: no engine is installed and enabled; a named engine: that one is missing or disabled). Off: the app stays available and searches natively where the model can.
edit.toolChoiceDesc: Whether the model decides for itself to use this app's tools
edit.toolChoiceRequiredHelp: The first answer step of every message must call one of the app's tools; the model can then answer from the result. Not every model can be forced by the provider - for those the model is asked in words instead.
edit.iassistantDesc: Configure iAssistant integration for this app
edit.iassistantProfileIdDesc: The iAssistant profile to use for this app (e.g., iassistant-workspace)
edit.iassistantSearchProfileDesc: The search profile to use for retrieval using iFinder (e.g., searchprofile-standard)
edit.iassistantAssistantIdDesc: An iAssistant from iFinder. It sets both the conversation profile and the search profile, and only users who have its search profile can use it. Leave empty to set the profiles below.
edit.iassistantAssistantLoadFailed: The iAssistants could not be loaded: {{error}}
edit.iassistantAssistantNoneVisible: iFinder shows you no iAssistants. You can still enter an ID.
edit.iassistantAllSearchProfiles: Search all of the user's search profiles
edit.iassistantAllSearchProfilesDesc: Sends no search profile, so iFinder searches everything the user may see through any of their search profiles. Requires iFinder 6.9 or later.
edit.iassistantExtraContextDesc: Additional context to be added to the response state prompt. Supports prompt variables like {{user_name}}, {{user_email}}, {{date}} and custom global variables. Use with care as changes can impact answer quality.
edit.iassistantSystemPromptPreambleDesc: The prompt preamble used in the response state system prompt. This is ideal for changing the identity of the iAssistant. Supports prompt variables like {{user_name}}, {{user_email}}, {{date}} and custom global variables. Use with care.
edit.iassistantChoosing: Choosing an iAssistant in the chat
edit.iassistantSwitchFixed: No, always use this app's setting
edit.iassistantOfferAllDesc: Users can then ask across every search profile they have.
edit.iassistantOfferAllOn: Always offered, because this app searches all of the user's search profiles.
edit.iassistantAskAction: Let other models ask this iAssistant
edit.iassistantAskActionDesc: For apps whose model is not the iAssistant: the model gets a tool to put questions to it. Off unless ticked.
edit.iassistantLegacyScope: This app sets scope values the panel does not manage: {{values}}.
edit.ifinderDesc: Let the model search iFinder, and choose the search profile users search in
edit.ifinderStartInDesc: The search profile a chat starts in. Empty: the installation's default search profile.
edit.ifinderLoadFailed: The search profiles could not be loaded: {{error}}
edit.ifinderNoneVisible: iFinder shows you no search profiles. You can still enter an ID.
edit.ifinderSwitchFixed: No, always use the start profile
edit.ifinderSwitchLocked: The iFinder installation does not let users change the search profile ("Users may change the search profile" is off), so every app searches in its default.
edit.skillsEnabledHelp: Skills are opt-in. When off, the app gets no skill list, no skill tools and no active skills, even if users own or are shared skills.
edit.skillsAllowPersonalHelp: Offer users' own and shared skills in addition to the skills listed above. Turn off to allow only the listed skills.
edit.noTranscriptionModels: No transcription models configured. Add one under Admin → Models (model type "transcription").
edit.trackedChangesHelp: How tracked changes in Word documents reach the model. Marked changes are written as {++added++} and {--removed--}.
edit.wordCommentsHelp: Whether comments in Word documents reach the model. They are written as {>>Author: text<<} after the text they belong to.
edit.speakerNotesHelp: Whether the speaker notes of PowerPoint and OpenDocument slides reach the model. They are written as [Notes] after the text of their slide.
edit.extractAudioFromVideo: Extract audio track (for transcription / audio models)
edit.maxVideoSizeHelp: Up to 51200 MB (50 GB). With audio extraction, an MP4 or MOV can be any size: only its audio is read. Other formats (WebM, MKV, ...) and videos sent as they are work up to 2 GB. Each file type has its own limit.
edit.appsAsToolsDesc: Let this app delegate to other apps. The model can call each selected app as a tool and use its answer (concierge pattern).
edit.appsAsToolsHelper: Each selected app becomes a tool (app__<id>) the model can call. Users only reach apps they have permission for, and a called app cannot call further apps.
edit.feedbackDesc: Let users rate this app’s responses with stars and an optional comment
edit.feedbackNote: When disabled, the star rating is hidden under this app’s responses and the feedback API rejects submissions for it. The platform-level feedback feature must also be enabled for the rating to appear; all of it is also manageable under Admin → Feedback.
edit.initialRowsHint: How tall the input is before the first message. Once the chat has started, the input is one line that grows as the user types.
edit.platformDefaultServiceHint: Follows the default set under Admin → Voice Input, including later changes.
edit.dictationModelHint: The microphone streams through the iHub server to this transcription model. Users need access to the model through their groups.
edit.dictationModelUnavailable: This model is disabled, no longer exists or does not stream, so voice input fails in this app.

voiceMode.title: Voice mode
voiceMode.description: A spoken conversation with this app: users talk and the app answers out loud. It listens with the speech recognition service above and speaks with a text-to-speech model.
voiceMode.needsMicrophone: Voice mode needs voice input. Enable the microphone above to use it in this app.
voiceMode.flagOff: Voice mode is a preview feature that is switched off under Admin → Features. These settings take effect once it is on.
voiceMode.label: Voice mode
voiceMode.defaultHint: Follows the setting under Admin → Voice Input, including later changes.
voiceMode.onHint: On for this app. Voice mode must also be switched on under Admin → Voice Input.
voiceMode.offHint: Voice mode is not offered in this app.
voiceMode.ttsModelHint: For example a German voice model for a German app. Users need access to the model through their groups.
voiceMode.ttsModelUnavailable: This model is disabled or no longer exists, so voice mode is not offered in this app.
voiceMode.voiceHint: Optional voice id of the text-to-speech model. Empty uses the voice settings of the model.

edit.websearchMaxPageReadsDesc: Caps how many pages the model may open with the page reader for one answer. Pages the search itself fetches for its excerpts do not count. 1–50, default 5.

usageGuide.title: Usage Guide
usageGuide.description: A pre-written answer to "How do I use this app?". Users open it in a dialog from the "Usage guide" link under the chat input. No model is called and the guide never enters the chat, so it costs nothing and leaves the context window free.
usageGuide.generateHint: Generating uses the default model once, with this form as it is now. Review the text — it is stored when you save the app.
usageGuide.question: Dialog heading
usageGuide.confirmRegenerate: Replace the current guide text for this language with a newly generated one?
usageGuide.confirmDelete: Delete the usage guide of this app?

edit.projectsDesc: Link admin projects whose knowledge this app uses. Choose per project whether it is loaded into the prompt, searched with tools, or decided automatically by size.
edit.projectsEnabledNote: When off, the app uses no project: neither the linked ones below nor chats started in a project or projects attached in the chat.
edit.userProjectsEnabledNote: Users can start chats of this app in their own projects and attach them in the chat. The platform-level personal projects feature must also be enabled.
edit.documentTemplateDesc: The corporate design of the PDF, Word and PowerPoint files this app creates (skills "pdf", "docx", "pptx") and of its PDF export.
edit.documentTemplatePinned: Every document of this app uses this template; the model cannot choose another one.
edit.documentTemplateFree: The default template applies; the model may use another template when the user asks for it.
edit.documentTemplateMissing: The template "{{id}}" does not exist; the default template applies.
edit.noLanguages: No languages configured. Add a language to get started.
edit.cloudStorageMoved: Files from storage providers (Office 365, Google Drive, Nextcloud): bind the providers under Integrations → Storage providers.
edit.toolApprovalHelp: Makes the approval stricter for this app. It can never relax the platform, tool or integration settings: a looser value is ignored.
edit.toolSearchHelp: When the tools of this app are too many for one request, the biggest integrations are left out and listed in the prompt; the model finds a tool with search_tools and the tools it finds are added to the request. Keeps requests small and tool choice sharp. Set "Always loaded" on an integration to keep it out of the search.
edit.toolSearchBudgetHelp: Tokens the tool definitions of one request may take before integrations are left to the search. Default 6000; never more than a tenth of the model's context window.

apps.reorderHelp: Drag a row or use the arrows to set the order apps appear in for users — in the apps browser, on the start page and in the sidebar. Every app is listed, so search and filters do not apply here. Nothing is saved until you choose "Save order".
apps.openAppHint: Open the app in a new tab
apps.openDisabledHint: Enable the app to open it

test.title: Test app
test.subtitle: Runs the saved version, as users see it
test.loadError: The app could not be loaded for the test.
test.unsavedHint: You have unsaved changes. Save to test them — the test restarts after every save.
test.chatOnly: Testing here works for chat apps. Use Open app to try this app.
test.disabled: This app is disabled, so it cannot be opened in the chat. Enable it and save to test it.

status.hiddenUntilFeature: Hidden from users until {{features}} is on

migrationWarnings.actionRemoved: The update of {{installation}} to v{{version}} removed the action “{{action}}”, which this app was bound to; the app no longer offers it.
migrationWarnings.typeBindingAction: The update of {{installation}} to v{{version}} renamed or removed the action “{{action}}”, which this app still names in its binding {{key}}: edit the binding.
migrationWarnings.typeBindingScope: The update of {{installation}} to v{{version}} renamed the scope “{{scope}}”, which this app still sets in its binding {{key}}: edit the binding.

aiNotice.title: AI notice
aiNotice.help: The notice is shown only in an empty chat. It is not saved and not sent to the AI.

integrationCatalog.catalogEmpty: No definitions match. Integrations can also be installed from the Marketplace.
integrationCatalog.unsupportedProtocol: This integration uses the protocol "{{protocol}}", which this release cannot run yet.

empty.title: Nothing installed yet
empty.description: Pick an integration from the catalog, enter its settings and test it before you save.

confirmRemove.title: Remove integration?
confirmRemove.message: Apps that use "{{id}}" lose its actions. An app that requires it is hidden from users until its configuration changes. A stored service-account token is deleted with it.

confirmDisable.title: Disable integration?
confirmDisable.message: Apps that use "{{id}}" go without it while it is disabled. An app that requires it is hidden from users.

authModes.serviceAccount: Shared service account (one token for everyone)
authModes.apiKeyUser: Each user enters an API key
authModes.oauthClient: iHub signs in with one OAuth client (client credentials)

wizard.instanceIdHelp: Apps refer to the installation by this id. Letters, digits, dots, hyphens.
wizard.label: Label
wizard.labelHelp: Shown to users in the chat, e.g. "GovData" or "Open Data Norderstedt".
wizard.secretStored: Stored. Leave empty to keep it.
wizard.needsToken: Needs a shared service account; off while sign-in is "none".
wizard.dynamicActionsEmpty: The server lists its tools when iHub connects. Test the connection to see them; every tool is on until you switch some off.
wizard.dynamicActionsUnavailable: The server did not list its tools (not reachable, or nobody connected yet). Saving keeps the stored tool selection as it is; test the connection to see and change it.
wizard.dynamicActionsHint: These are the tools the server lists; a tool the server adds later is on by default.
wizard.dynamicActionsAllowlistHint: These are the tools the server lists; only the checked ones may run, and a tool the server adds later stays off until you switch it on.
wizard.runsCode: This integration runs its own connector module in the iHub server process. Install it only from a publisher you trust.
wizard.descriptionHelp: What this installation holds, for admins and — where the integration reads it, like a people directory — for the model: say what is in it and what to search by.
wizard.alwaysInstalledHelp: This integration is always installed and enabled; switch single actions off below instead.

connections.title: Connected users
connections.empty: Nobody has connected their account yet.
connections.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect "{{user}}" from {{label}}? They have to sign in again to use it.
connections.resetConfirm: Reset the OAuth client registration of {{label}}? The next sign-in registers iHub afresh; connected users may have to connect again.

integrationCatalog.incompatibleReason: This installation offers no actions: its definition {{reason}}.
integrationCatalog.marketplaceOff: The catalog also lists the integrations of the marketplace (hosted MCP servers such as GitHub, Linear or Stripe) when the Marketplace feature is on under Admin → Features.

websiteCorpusDomains.title: Internal websites for the Website Corpus
websiteCorpusDomains.description: The server refuses company-internal addresses. Users whose crawl was refused can ask for the host here. An approval lets the Website Corpus reach that host only; other tools keep the public-addresses-only rule. Loopback, link-local and cloud metadata addresses can never be allowed.
websiteCorpusDomains.loadFailed: The internal websites could not be loaded.
websiteCorpusDomains.addTitle: Allow a host without a request
websiteCorpusDomains.hostHelp: A host name or address, or a wildcard such as *.corp.example for every host below a domain.

nextcloudEmbed.title: Nextcloud Embed
nextcloudEmbed.description: Embed iHub inside Nextcloud. Users start a chat from Nextcloud Files with documents pre-attached, similar to the Outlook add-in.

copilotAgent.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot
copilotAgent.description: Make iHub an agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot. Copilot runs iHub's apps through the MCP gateway, signed in with the user's iHub account.

outlook.title: Outlook Add-in
outlook.description: Embed iHub apps inside the Outlook task pane. Users sign in with their iHub account and run prompts against the currently selected email.

browserExtension.title: Browser Extension
browserExtension.description: Side-panel extension for Chrome / Edge / Firefox. Run any iHub app against the page the user is reading.

mcpGateway.title: MCP gateway
mcpGateway.description: Let external MCP clients use iHub's apps as tools, signed in through iHub's own OAuth server.

integrations.featureFlagOff: The "integrations" feature flag is off. Enable it under Admin → Features to surface integration endpoints to clients.
integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.subtitle: The systems iHub works with: install an integration from the catalog, point it at your system and bind it to apps. Inbound lists what connects to iHub.

page.definitionMissing: The definition "{{definition}}" of this installation is not loaded: it offers no actions and cannot be edited. Install the definition again from the marketplace, or remove the installation.
page.noLiveActions: The system lists its actions when iHub connects. Test the connection to see them.
page.noActions: This integration offers no actions to the model; apps use it through their own settings.
page.noApps: No app binds this installation yet. Bind it in an app’s Integrations section.

via.webSearchAuto: web search on Auto (the first engine a user may use)

page.notEditable: This installation cannot be edited while its definition is missing or incompatible.

clients.description: Where users work with iHub outside the web app: Outlook, the browser, Nextcloud and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Each one is set up on its own page.

webSearch.description: Search engines apps with web search on use; without one, models search natively where they can.

storage.title: Storage providers
storage.description: Cloud storage users browse and attach files from in the chat and in projects.

mcp.description: Model Context Protocol servers; their tools are the actions.

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: Remote agents (A2A) the model hands tasks to; their skills are the actions.

builtIn.description: Integrations that ship with iHub, such as iFinder, iAssistant and Jira.

custom.description: Integrations built here with "Add manually", and the tools migrated from the former Tools page.

iassistant.connectionRequired: Pick the iFinder installation iAssistant runs on.
iassistant.connectionSectionHelp: iAssistant uses the base URL and the sign-in of an iFinder installation; configure those there.
iassistant.defaultProfileIdHelp: The iAssistant profile used when an app names none (plain text or base64 encoded).
iassistant.defaultSearchProfileHelp: The search profile iAssistant conversations search when neither the app nor the model names one.
iassistant.testHelp: The test reaches iAssistant through the selected iFinder installation as your own admin account, with the values above (unsaved).

webSearch.engineSectionHelp: Apps with web search on use this engine when they name it, or on Auto when it is the first engine a user may use (Brave, Staan, Qwant, then any other engine). Models with native search do not need an engine.
webSearch.apiKeyHelp: A credential of type secret holding the {{engine}} API key. Add one under Admin → Integrations → Credentials.
webSearch.envFallback: Without a credential, the server uses the environment variable {{env}} when it is set. A picked credential always wins.
webSearch.egressHint: Qwant blocks many data-centre IP addresses. Run Test connection to see whether it answers this server.
webSearch.testHelp: The test checks the API key of the values above (unsaved) and runs one live search from this server.

ifinder.privateKeyHelp: The stored credential holding the RSA or EC private key (PEM) that signs the iFinder JWT. Alternatively set the IFINDER_PRIVATE_KEY environment variable on the server.
ifinder.effectiveIssuerAutoHelp: Detected from your server URL. Set a custom issuer under Admin → OAuth Server if needed.
ifinder.oidcKeyPairMissingIssuerHelp: Set the OAuth issuer URL under Admin → Authentication → OAuth Server before saving.

info.title: iFinder JWT authentication
info.description: Every call runs as the signed-in user: iHub signs a JWT for the user, or exchanges the user’s sign-in token at a shared OIDC provider. iAssistant runs on this connection.

ifinder.baseUrlHelp: Your iFinder / iAssistant server; the API paths are appended.

authMode.label: Token issuer
authMode.oidcTokenExchangeHelp: iHub and iFinder share one OIDC provider. iHub keeps the sign-in token of each user and exchanges it at the provider for a token for iFinder. Users must sign in to iHub through that provider; background runs use the stored refresh token.
authMode.ihubSignedHelp: iHub signs the iFinder token itself, with a private key or the iHub OIDC key pair. iFinder trusts iHub as the issuer.

ifinder.useOidcKeyPair: Sign with the iHub OIDC key pair
ifinder.useOidcKeyPairHelp: Tokens are signed with the RSA key of the iHub OIDC server. iFinder validates them through JWKS discovery (/.well-known/jwks.json); no key has to be distributed. Prerequisite: your iFinder instance must already trust iHub as a JWT issuer via its JWKS endpoint (/.well-known/jwks.json). Without this iFinder-side configuration the connection fails with a 401 error.
ifinder.jwtSubjectFieldHelp: The "sub" claim of the iFinder JWT: which user attribute identifies the user, as iFinder knows them.
ifinder.searchSectionHelp: Which iFinder search profile a chat searches, and which ones users may pick.
ifinder.defaultSearchProfileHelp: The search profile a chat searches until the user picks another one.
ifinder.allowedSearchProfilesHelp: One search profile id per line. Empty offers every profile the user has in iFinder.
ifinder.allowUserSearchProfileChange: Users may change the search profile
ifinder.allowUserSearchProfileChangeHelp: Off: every chat searches the default search profile, and neither the user nor the model can pick another.
ifinder.advancedToggle: Request timeout, download directory and API paths

diagnostics.exchangeDescription: The test exchanges your own stored sign-in token at the OIDC provider and calls the endpoints the integration uses, with the values above (unsaved). It always runs as you: the exchange needs your sign-in.
diagnostics.description: The test signs a JWT for your own admin account and calls the endpoints the integration uses, with the values above (unsaved).

tokenExchange.noProviders: No OIDC provider is configured. Add the provider iFinder uses under Admin → Authentication first.
tokenExchange.providerHelp: The provider iHub and iFinder share. Its sign-in tokens are kept (encrypted) and exchanged for iFinder tokens with the client ID and secret configured for it under Admin → Authentication. Add "offline_access" to its scopes so background runs keep working.
tokenExchange.audienceObo: Not used by On-Behalf-Of: Entra takes the audience from the scope (api://<ifinder-app-id>/.default).
tokenExchange.audienceHelp: The client or project id of iFinder at the provider. The issued token carries it as "aud".
tokenExchange.scopeMapHelp: Translates the scopes iHub asks for into the scopes of the provider (Zitadel role scopes, Entra api://…/.default). An empty value sends the iHub scope unchanged.
tokenExchange.extraScopesHelp: Space-separated scopes sent with every exchange.
tokenExchange.ifinderSetupHelp: The token iHub sends must also carry the fa_* claims iFinder reads, either as requested scopes or added by a claim mapper on the provider. The connection test shows which ones are present.
tokenExchange.providerRequired: Select the OIDC provider iHub shares with iFinder.

ifinder.oidcKeyPairNeedsIssuer: Signing with the OIDC key pair needs an OAuth issuer URL. It is detected from your server URL, or set it under Admin → Authentication → OAuth Server.

editors.nameSectionHelp: How users see this integration in the chat. The id stays fixed.
editors.actionsSectionHelp: An app that binds this integration offers the checked actions; it can narrow them further.

source.description: Where the directory lives and how iHub reaches it.
source.directHelp: For directories without a sign-in provider, such as the external x500.bund.de.
source.missingProvider: The sign-in provider "{{name}}" is not configured. Save it in the authentication settings first, or choose another one.
source.noProviders: No LDAP sign-in provider is configured.
source.overridesHelp: Leave a field empty to use the value of the sign-in provider.
source.presetHelp: Sets which entries are people and where each field is read from. See Search and mapping below.
source.reuseHelp: URL, base DN, directory type and bind account come from an LDAP sign-in provider of the authentication settings.
source.starttlsHelp: Upgrades an ldap:// connection to TLS before anything is searched. Not needed for ldaps://.
source.title: Source
source.urlHelp: ldaps://host:636 for TLS. ldap://host:389 needs StartTLS — or plain text allowed under Network, which is not recommended.

access.anonymousHelp: Only for directories that allow anonymous search, such as x500.bund.de. Active Directory normally does not.
access.description: How iHub signs in to the directory. Searches never run with a user's own password, because iHub does not keep it.
access.noBindAccount: This sign-in provider has no bind account. Choose anonymous access if the directory allows it, or a service account.
access.passwordHelp: Choose the stored credential that holds the password.
access.providerAccountHelp: The service account the provider already uses to look up users.
access.serviceHelp: A read-only account of its own for the people search.
access.servicePlaintext: A service account never binds over plain text. Use ldaps:// or StartTLS, or this directory cannot connect.
access.title: Access

network.allowedHostsHelp: One host per line. iHub refuses a directory host that resolves to a private, loopback or link-local address unless it is listed here or in the platform-wide SSRF allow-list. The host of a reused sign-in provider is always allowed.
network.description: How the connection is secured and which servers iHub may reach.
network.plaintextRefused: This directory uses ldap:// without StartTLS. iHub refuses the connection until plain text is allowed here — better switch to ldaps:// or StartTLS.
network.plaintextWarning: Without TLS, the search terms and the records the directory returns — names, phone numbers, e-mail addresses — cross the network in plain text. Use ldaps://host:636, or ldap://host:389 with StartTLS, whenever the server supports it. A service account password is never sent in plain text.
network.title: Network
network.tlsCaHelp: Only for a CA that the iHub server does not trust already. One name per line: the file contents/config/certs/<name>.pem on the server. When set, only these certificates verify the server's certificate. Leave empty to use the public roots and the server's operating system certificate store. Verification stays on unless the host is on the platform's SSL whitelist.
network.tlsCiphersHelp: An OpenSSL cipher list. Empty: Node's defaults. These are the only TLS settings a directory may change; a reused sign-in provider's values for them apply unless set here.

visibility.title: Visibility
visibility.description: Who may search this directory, and where the search terms go.
visibility.internalHelp: The directory is run by your organisation.
visibility.externalHelp: A third party runs the directory, so the names users search for leave your organisation. Say so in the description, too.
visibility.groupsHelp: A group grants this directory by its id, by "People directory (LDAP)", by "All people directories" or by "*". Apps and tool permissions cannot widen this.

model.description: The model chooses a directory by these texts. Say whose staff it lists, which fields it has, and whether it is an external service.
model.name: Name
model.noDescription: Without a description the model knows nothing but the name and id, and may pick the wrong directory.
model.title: Model-facing name and description

limits.description: Upper bounds for each search. A tool call can ask for fewer results, never more. All tools of this directory, its test and the LDAP browsers that reuse it share one request queue.
limits.title: Limits
limits.unitsHelp: Lists the units directly below the search base (for x500.bund.de: the authorities), so the model can narrow a search to one of them.

mapping.description: Defaults come from the directory type "{{preset}}". Leave a field empty to keep the preset value shown next to it.
mapping.fieldsHelp: Comma-separated candidates; the first one with a value wins. A candidate is an attribute (mail), a component of the entry’s DN (dn:l), or attributes joined by a space (givenName sn). Only mapped attributes are read from the directory.
mapping.searchAttributesHelp: Comma-separated, at most 12. Each word of a search is matched against these attributes.
mapping.searchBaseHelp: Where people are searched. Defaults to the base DN.
mapping.title: Search and mapping

transport.plaintextHint: Search terms and results cross the network unencrypted.

errors.urlPattern: Use ldaps://host:636 or ldap://host:389, without a path.
errors.passwordRefRequired: Choose the credential that holds the password.
errors.tlsCaPattern: "{{name}}" is not a certificate name: use lower-case letters, digits and "-", without ".pem".
errors.personFilterPattern: An LDAP filter in parentheses, e.g. (objectClass=person).
errors.attributeName: "{{name}}" is not an LDAP attribute name.
errors.limitRange: Enter a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.

peopleDirectory.statusTitle: As saved, this directory has issues:
peopleDirectory.testHelp: Checks the configuration, the address, the connection, StartTLS and the bind with the values above (unsaved). With a name, it also runs a search and shows the mapped people next to the attributes they came from. Nothing is saved.
peopleDirectory.testQueryHelp: Optional: a name to search for, to check the mapping.

ldapBrowser.directorySectionHelp: The browser uses the connection of a People directory (LDAP) installation: its URL, TLS settings, trusted certificates, allowed hosts, base DN and, unless you give the browser an account of its own, its bind account.
ldapBrowser.directoryMissingHint: The directory "{{id}}" is not installed: the browser offers no tools. Choose another one.
ldapBrowser.noDirectories: No People directory (LDAP) is installed. Install one under Integrations first.
ldapBrowser.directoryDisabled: This directory is disabled. The browser offers its tools only while the directory is enabled.
ldapBrowser.settingsSectionHelp: Lets admins ask about the directory in plain words and see the raw entries: attributes, branches, group members. Separate from people search, which only returns mapped fields.
ldapBrowser.baseHelp: Every DN the browser reads must lie here. Leave empty for the directory's base DN, the whole directory; set a branch to limit what admins can see.
ldapBrowser.bindDirectoryHelp: The account the directory searches with. The browser can read everything it can read.
ldapBrowser.bindAnonymousHelp: Only what the directory shows to anonymous clients.
ldapBrowser.bindServiceHelp: A read-only account with exactly the reach admins should have.
ldapBrowser.bindDirectoryWarning: With the directory's account, the browser has the full reach of the people search account. Use an account of its own if that account can read more than admins should see.
ldapBrowser.passwordHelp: Choose the stored credential that holds the password.
ldapBrowser.servicePlaintext: A service account never binds over plain text. Use ldaps:// or StartTLS on the directory, or the browser cannot connect.
ldapBrowser.denyAttributesHelp: One attribute name per line. Passwords, LAPS and BitLocker secrets, certificates and photos are always withheld; add attributes where your directory keeps other secrets. Withheld attributes cannot be used in a filter either.
ldapBrowser.auditNote: Every browser call is written to the audit log with the filter used, never the values returned. The browser is never offered over the MCP gateway. The LDAP browser app ships disabled: enable it under Apps and give it only to admin groups.
ldapBrowser.accessNote: Only signed-in users browse. Personal API keys, OAuth clients and agents never do, whatever their groups. Raw entries are not for everyone: grant this browser to admin groups only, not with "*".

errors.directoryRequired: Choose the people directory whose connection the browser uses.
errors.limitRange: Enter a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
errors.passwordRefRequired: Choose the credential that holds the password.
errors.attributeName: "{{name}}" is not an LDAP attribute name.

ldapBrowser.testHelp: Checks the directory it reuses, the address, the connection, StartTLS and the bind with the browser's account, and lists the entries directly under the browse base, with the values above (unsaved).

entra.registrationSectionHelp: iHub looks people up through Microsoft Graph with the client credentials of an app registration, not as the signed-in user. Grant the registration the application permissions User.Read.All and GroupMember.Read.All, with admin consent.
entra.tenantIdHelp: The directory (tenant) id of your Entra ID tenant.
entra.clientIdHelp: The app registration that holds the Graph application permissions.
entra.clientSecretHelp: A credential of type secret holding the app registration's client secret (Admin → Credentials). The secret is never stored in the installation.
entra.envUsed: Empty: {{variable}} is used (set on the server).
entra.envMissing: Empty, and {{variable}} is not set on the server.
entra.envFallback: Empty: the environment variable {{variable}} is used.
entra.notGuid: This does not look like an id from Entra ID (a GUID).
entra.incomplete: Without {{fields}} the directory cannot sign in: fill the fields, or set the environment variables on the server.
entra.testHelp: Fetches a token with the values above (unsaved), falling back to the AZURE_* variables, and reads one user through Microsoft Graph.

storage.registerSectionHelp: The provider sends users back to this URL after they sign in. It contains the installation id "{{id}}", which never changes.

register.office365: Azure portal → Microsoft Entra ID → App registrations → your app → Authentication → Platform "Web" → Redirect URIs.
register.googledrive: Google Cloud console → APIs & Services → Credentials → your OAuth 2.0 client (Web application) → Authorized redirect URIs.
register.nextcloud: Nextcloud → Administration settings → Security → OAuth 2.0 clients → add a client with this redirect URI.

storage.redirectDerivedHelp: Derived the way the server derives it from each request: this address, the base path and the callback path. Set the field below when the provider must see a different address (an unusual proxy setup).
storage.redirectConfiguredHelp: The configured redirect URI below is used for every sign-in.
storage.redirectUriHelp: Leave empty to derive it from each request (recommended).

oauthSectionHelp.office365: The Azure app registration users sign in with (Microsoft Graph, delegated permissions).
oauthSectionHelp.googledrive: The OAuth 2.0 client (Web application) of your Google Cloud project, with the Drive API enabled.
oauthSectionHelp.nextcloud: The Nextcloud server and the OAuth 2.0 client registered in it.

storage.serverUrlHelp: The base URL of the instance (no trailing slash); the base for OAuth, OCS and WebDAV.
storage.tenantIdHelp: An identifier, not a secret: stored in the installation as plain text.
storage.clientSecretHelp: A credential of type secret holding the client secret (Admin → Integrations → Credentials).

sourcesSectionHelp.office365: Sign-in asks only for the Microsoft Graph permissions the checked sources need; switch off what your tenant does not consent to.
sourcesSectionHelp.googledrive: The picker offers only the checked sources.

sources.personalDriveHelp: Asks for Files.Read only, which users consent to themselves.
sources.followedSitesHelp: Asks for Sites.Read.All and Files.Read.All (admin consent).
sources.teamsHelp: Asks for Team.ReadBasic.All, Channel.ReadBasic.All and Files.Read.All (admin consent).

storage.noSource: No source is checked: users can connect but browse nothing.
storage.siteUrlHelp: Restrict access to one SharePoint site.
storage.connectionsSectionHelp: Every user connects their own account, under Settings → Integrations or from the file picker. Connections are stored per installation.
storage.statusEnabled: Enabled: users whose groups grant it can connect.
storage.statusDisabled: Disabled: users cannot connect or pick files from it.
storage.testHelp: Checks the values above (unsaved): client and secret, the provider settings, the redirect URI, whether the provider answers, and how many users are connected. Signing in needs a browser: connect under Settings → Integrations.

required.tenantId: Enter the Directory (tenant) ID of the app registration.
required.clientId: Enter the client ID of the OAuth app.
required.clientSecretRef: Pick the credential that holds the client secret.
required.serverUrl: Enter the URL of the Nextcloud server.

errors.redirectPath: The redirect URI has to end in {{path}}.

access.noGroup: No group grants it yet: nobody can use it.
access.help: Groups decide which integrations their members may use (inherited like apps).

warnings.actionRemoved: The action “{{action}}” is removed from the app “{{app}}” (binding {{key}}); the app no longer offers it.
warnings.typeBindingAction: The app “{{app}}” names the action “{{action}}” in its type binding {{key}}, which is shared with other definitions and not rewritten: edit the app.
warnings.typeBindingScope: The app “{{app}}” sets the scope “{{scope}}” in its type binding {{key}}, which is shared with other definitions and not rewritten: edit the app.
warnings.moduleNotPlanned: The migration runs the code module {{module}}; what it changes is known only when it runs and is not counted here.

log.title: Migration log
log.empty: No migration has run for this installation.

restore.title: Restore a backup of {{label}}?
restore.message: The installation’s values, its action policy and the bindings of its apps go back to the backup {{backup}} (v{{version}}, taken {{date}}). What changed since then is replaced; iHub backs up the current state first.
restore.definition: The backup also holds the definition of v{{version}}; when the loaded definition is another version, it is put back too.

adopt.title: Adopt v{{version}} for {{label}}?
adopt.message: You confirm that the stored values already fit {{definition}} v{{version}}. iHub checks them like the result of a migration and only then records the version; no value is changed. Values that do not fit are listed and nothing is recorded.

revert.title: Revert {{label}} to v{{version}}?
revert.message: The installation’s values, its action policy, the bindings of its apps and its marketplace entry go back to the backup {{backup}} (v{{version}}, taken {{date}}). What changed since then is replaced; iHub backs up the current state first, so you can revert forward again.
revert.definition: The definition goes back to v{{version}} too. Other installations of the same definition follow it: each gets its own backup of v{{version}} restored, or needs a review.

outcome.migrated: {{label}} was migrated from v{{from}} to v{{to}}.
outcome.stamped: {{label}} now records v{{to}}; no migration had to run.

outcome.restored: The backup {{backup}} of {{label}} was restored; it is at v{{to}} again.

panel.title: Definition migration
panel.pending: {{definition}} v{{to}} is loaded; this installation records v{{from}}. Until it is migrated it offers no actions and its settings cannot be saved.
panel.pendingStamp: {{definition}} v{{to}} is loaded; this installation records v{{from}}. No migration lies between the versions, so it keeps working: Migrate now (or the next save) records v{{to}}.
panel.failed: The migration to v{{to}} failed and changed nothing: the values are still those of v{{from}}. The installation offers no actions until you re-run the migration, restore the backup or uninstall it.
panel.downgrade: The loaded definition v{{to}} is older than this installation’s v{{from}} (a downgrade). Migrations only run forward, so the installation offers no actions until you restore the backup of v{{to}}, adopt v{{to}} or uninstall it.
panel.review: iHub cannot tell which definition version the values of this installation were written for. It offers no actions until you restore a backup, adopt the loaded version v{{to}} or uninstall it.
panel.changes: The migrations {{migrations}} change {{changes}}; a backup is made first.
panel.noChanges: The migrations {{migrations}} change nothing this installation stores; a backup is made first.
panel.notPlanned: The migrations {{migrations}} run; what they change could not be planned in advance. A backup is made first.
panel.collisionsHelp: A step would overwrite something that already exists. Remove the destination first (for example in the app), or the migration fails and changes nothing.
panel.errorsTitle: The result would not fit v{{to}}: the migration will fail
panel.noBackup: No backup of this installation matches its state, so there is nothing to restore.

migration.settingsReadOnly: The settings are read-only until the migration state is resolved: iHub refuses to save values that were written for another definition version. Use the actions of the migration panel above.

refreshTtl.label: Refresh files and web pages after
refreshTtl.help: Files and web pages from websites are fetched again after this time; an unchanged one keeps its text. Projects and items can set their own.

refreshMode.label: Refresh outdated files and web pages
refreshMode.help: Always: refreshed in the background, used or not. Automatically: refreshed in the background while a project is used. When the project is used: outdated ones are not refreshed in the background; using the project (a chat, a search, an app or a workflow reading it, attaching it to a chat; not opening it) refreshes what is outdated, and answers use the stored text until then. Projects and items can set their own.

refreshIdleDays.label: Refresh only when used after (days without use)
refreshIdleDays.help: For "Automatically, while the project is used": a project nobody used for this many days is no longer refreshed in the background, only when it is used again. 0 always refreshes in the background.

refreshWait.label: Wait for outdated documents before answering (seconds)
refreshWait.help: Before a chat or a workflow reads a project, its outdated files and web pages are refreshed and waited for up to this long. What is not done by then is read as stored and keeps refreshing. 0 answers at once from what is stored.

fetchConcurrency.label: Files and web pages checked at once
fetchConcurrency.help: Per server process. Checking whether a file or page changed takes little memory; at least as many as conversions at once.

convertConcurrency.label: Documents converted at once
convertConcurrency.help: Per server process: uploads, and files and web pages that changed, are read into text this many at a time. Each conversion can take a lot of memory.

indexEntries.label: Search indexes kept in memory
indexEntries.help: Per server process, one per project. A project whose index is not in memory is indexed again on its next question, which takes 60 to 90 ms of processing time for a large project. Raise it when many projects are in use at the same time.

indexShare.label: Memory share of the search indexes (%)
indexShare.help: Share of the server process's memory the indexes may use. Empty: 10 %, at most about 135 MB.

textShare.label: Memory share of the cached document texts (%)
textShare.help: Share of the server process's memory the decrypted texts may use. Empty: 6 %, at most 96 MB.

caches.hint: Each server process (worker) holds its own copy, so memory grows with the number of workers. A share you enter replaces the built-in maximum. Check the cache metrics before raising it.

settings.title: Provenance settings
settings.description: How long output records are kept, who may check an output, and how strict the watermark detector is. Changes apply immediately; no restart is needed. Every save is written to the audit log.
settings.storeRecords: Keep a record of every output
settings.storeRecordsHelp: A record holds a hash of the output, never its text. Without records, "did this installation produce this text?" cannot be answered. Default: on.
settings.retentionHelp: 0 keeps records forever. Older records are deleted by a daily clean-up.
settings.accessAuthenticatedHelp: Anonymous visitors get a sign-in request. Default.
settings.accessPublicHelp: Third parties such as journalists or platforms can check a text or file. Anyone can then find out whether a text came from this installation.
settings.maxVerify: Largest file that can be checked
settings.maxVerifyHelp: Applies to image and audio uploads on the check form. Larger files are refused.
settings.readC2paHelp: Reads the provider mark (C2PA manifest) of generated and uploaded images. Default: on.
settings.detectionIntro: Leave a field empty to use its default. The defaults suit most installations; change them only for a reason.
settings.alphaHelp: The chance that a text is wrongly called "consistent with our watermark". Smaller is stricter. Between 0 and 1, for example 0.0001.
settings.minTokens: Shortest text that can be judged
settings.minTokensHelp: Shorter texts are reported as "too short to tell" instead of "not watermarked".
settings.timeoutHelp: How long to wait for the detector of a model. Between 1000 and 120000.
settings.saved: Settings saved. They apply now; no restart needed.
settings.fixErrors: Fix the marked fields and save again.
settings.confirmRetention: Records older than {{days}} days are deleted at the next daily clean-up. This cannot be undone, and those outputs can no longer be recognised.
settings.confirmPublic: Anyone on the internet can then check texts and files against this installation without signing in.
settings.confirmRestricted: Third parties who rely on checking without an account will be asked to sign in.
settings.recordUserHelp: Applies to records written from now on. Only admins see it when checking an output; it is never part of what a user or API caller receives. It stays in the record when the user is deleted.
settings.recordUserNoneHelp: The record describes the output only. Default.
settings.recordUserAnonymousHelp: A hash keyed with a secret only the server holds (usr_…). Records of one person share the value, but the user cannot be determined from it.
settings.recordUserPseudonymousHelp: A plain SHA-256 of the user id. Whoever knows a user id can compute it and so attribute the record.
settings.recordUserIdentifiedHelp: The user id, never the name or email. The records then hold personal data: cover them in your data protection documentation.
